entity-ungrouped-transition-morphscene-entity-transitions0 of 0.75 (major)failI&#39;m ruling Judge A&#39;s fail. The requirement is that an entity with the same identity in two consecutive steps animates from its old state to its new state in place. The guidance says to judge the kit&#39;s ungrouped step transition together with the kit primitives that render the persisting entity. Stage keys its scene wrapper by `groupKey ?? step.id` (Stage.tsx:28). Two consecutive steps with no shared group therefore mount a new scene instance while the old one exits, inside a sync-mode AnimatePresence with the exiting wrapper taken out of flow (Stage.tsx:50-64). Only primitives that carry a shared `layoutId` can carry an entity across that remount. MotionNode does (MotionNode.tsx:14-16). The kit&#39;s Arrow primitive does not. It takes an identity `id` but only writes it to `data-presentation-id` (Arrow.tsx:62-63). It never sets `layoutId` or `layout`. Its geometry is animated only by the `d` interpolation on `motion.path` with `initial={false}` (Arrow.tsx:76-79), which can only interpolate while the same component instance stays mounted. Across an ungrouped transition, the incoming Arrow is a fresh instance. Its paths start at the new geometry, and its svg fades in from `initial={{ opacity: 0 }}` over ENTER_T (Arrow.tsx:70-73). Meanwhile the old Arrow fades out with the exiting scene. So the arrow is never animated from its old endpoints to its new ones in place: the old copy disappears while a new copy fades in at the destination. That is the &#39;vanishes and reappears instead of morphing&#39; failure the guidance names, so the clause &#39;animates that entity from its old state … to its new state in place&#39; is unmet for Arrow entities. Judges B and C are right that Stage uses sync mode with no mode=&quot;wait&quot;, that the exiting wrapper is taken out of flow, and that MotionNode has no opacity hiding or delay. But they judged only the MotionNode-based primitives. They never looked at Arrow, which is also a kit entity primitive with a stable id. A pass needs every primitive that renders a persisting entity to keep it visible and morph it, so their reasoning does not decide the requirement. Arrow fails it. The delivered sample puts all nine steps in one group (steps/index.ts:7-12), but that does not change the kit behavior this criterion targets: the guidance explicitly names the ungrouped transition.Stage.tsx:28 keys the scene by `step.groupKey ?? step.id`, so ungrouped consecutive steps remount separate scene instances. | Stage.tsx:51-59: sync-mode AnimatePresence. The svg starts at opacity 0 and fades in over ENTER_T (0.4s, constants.ts:10). | Arrow.tsx:76-79: paths use `initial={false}` with an animated `d`. engineering-typed-kit-primitivesengineering-presentation-code-and-tests0.375 of 0.375 (minor)passI&#39;m ruling with judge B (pass). The three clauses hold. (1) Typed props: every public primitive exported from index.ts has an explicit typed interface. Box, Label, Frame, Emphasis and SymbolChip use NodeProps (id: string, at?: At, className?: string, style?: CSSProperties, variant?: string, children?: ReactNode). Arrow, Appear and SceneLayer use ArrowProps, AppearProps and SceneLayerProps. None is an untyped bag such as Record&lt;string, unknown&gt;, which is the fail trigger the guidance names for this clause. (2) Identity hooks cannot be overridden: MotionNode destructures a fixed set of fields and builds layoutId, data-presentation-node, data-presentation-id and data-variant itself, with no caller spread on the rendered element. Arrow and SceneLayer set their data-presentation-* hooks directly. SceneLayer spreads only the caller&#39;s style object. Appear accepts no caller element props. (3) Kit-only props stay off the DOM: `at` is used only by placement(); Box pulls `Icon` out and renders it as a child; `kind` and `tag` are used only to pick the hook value and the element; Arrow&#39;s from, to, bend, bidirectional, designW and designH go into path math and sizing. Judge A fails clause 1 because the interfaces are bespoke rather than inherited element props. The guidance&#39;s trigger for that clause is an untyped bag in place of the element&#39;s props, and it says typed primitives that apply hooks safely and strip kit-only props pass. A hand-written typed interface is not an untyped bag, so A&#39;s reason does not decide the requirement. Judge C says Box&#39;s `{...props}` after `kind=&quot;box&quot;` lets a caller override data-presentation-node. Box&#39;s rest props are typed as NodeProps minus Icon and children, and NodeProps has no `kind` or `tag` field. Label, Frame, Emphasis and SymbolChip likewise take only NodeProps, so TypeScript&#39;s JSX excess-property check rejects a caller passing `kind`. No source in the candidate passes it, so C&#39;s scenario is a hypothetical input the cited source does not produce. The requirement is that an entity with the same identity in two consecutive steps animates from its old state to its new state in place. The guidance says to judge the kit&#39;s ungrouped step transition together with the kit primitives that render the persisting entity. Stage keys its scene wrapper by `groupKey ?? step.id` (Stage.tsx:28). Two consecutive steps with no shared group therefore mount a new scene instance while the old one exits, inside a sync-mode AnimatePresence with the exiting wrapper taken out of flow (Stage.tsx:50-64). Only primitives that carry a shared `layoutId` can carry an entity across that remount. MotionNode does (MotionNode.tsx:14-16). The kit&#39;s Arrow primitive does not. It takes an identity `id` but only writes it to `data-presentation-id` (Arrow.tsx:62-63). It never sets `layoutId` or `layout`. Its geometry is animated only by the `d` interpolation on `motion.path` with `initial={false}` (Arrow.tsx:76-79), which can only interpolate while the same component instance stays mounted. Across an ungrouped transition, the incoming Arrow is a fresh instance. Its paths start at the new geometry, and its svg fades in from `initial={{ opacity: 0 }}` over ENTER_T (Arrow.tsx:70-73). Meanwhile the old Arrow fades out with the exiting scene. So the arrow is never animated from its old endpoints to its new ones in place: the old copy disappears while a new copy fades in at the destination. That is the &#39;vanishes and reappears instead of morphing&#39; failure the guidance names, so the clause &#39;animates that entity from its old state … to its new state in place&#39; is unmet for Arrow entities. Judges B and C are right that Stage uses sync mode with no mode=&quot;wait&quot;, that the exiting wrapper is taken out of flow, and that MotionNode has no opacity hiding or delay. But they judged only the MotionNode-based primitives. They never looked at Arrow, which is also a kit entity primitive with a stable id. A pass needs every primitive that renders a persisting entity to keep it visible and morph it, so their reasoning does not decide the requirement. Arrow fails it. The delivered sample puts all nine steps in one group (steps/index.ts:7-12), but that does not change the kit behavior this criterion targets: the guidance explicitly names the ungrouped transition.","evidence":["Stage.tsx:28 keys the scene by `step.groupKey ?? step.id`, so ungrouped consecutive steps remount separate scene instances.","Stage.tsx:51-59: sync-mode AnimatePresence. The guidance says to judge the kit&#39;s ungrouped step transition together with the kit primitives that render the persisting entity. Stage keys its scene wrapper by `groupKey ?? step.id` (Stage.tsx:28). Two consecutive steps with no shared group therefore mount a new scene instance while the old one exits, inside a sync-mode AnimatePresence with the exiting wrapper taken out of flow (Stage.tsx:50-64). Meanwhile the old Arrow fades out with the exiting scene. So the arrow is never animated from its old endpoints to its new ones in place: the old copy disappears while a new copy fades in at the destination. The orphaned `node scripts/verify.mjs` process therefore keeps running instead of being killed. The auditor says the script&#39;s finally cleanup never runs, but that does not follow. After the preview starts, every wait in `verify.mjs` has a bound: readiness has a 30 s deadline, `waitForSelector` 10 s, step transitions 4 s, text reads 2 s, and Playwright&#39;s default navigation timeout applies. Every exit path then reaches `finally { await browser?.close(); preview.stop() }`, and `stop()` kills the detached process group with `process.kill(-child.pid, &#39;SIGKILL&#39;)`. Also, `exec()` resolves on the child&#39;s &#39;close&#39; event, which waits until all inherited stdio pipes close. In practice that means the test waits for the orphaned verify process to finish. This timeout is also a hypothetical exit path that the recorded runs never hit. The guidance&#39;s failure case is a test that kills only the wrapper and leaves the preview running, and the material does not show that outcome.
